formats.key: PermitWitnessTransferFrom(TokenPermissions permitted,address spender,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline,ExclusiveDutchOrder witness)DutchOutput(address token,uint256 startAmount,uint256 endAmount,address recipient)ExclusiveDutchOrder(OrderInfo info,uint256 decayStartTime,uint256 decayEndTime,address exclusiveFiller,uint256 exclusivityOverrideBps,address inputToken,uint256 inputStartAmount,uint256 inputEndAmount,DutchOutput[] outputs)OrderInfo(address reactor,address swapper,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline,address additionalValidationContract,bytes additionalValidationData)TokenPermissions(address token,uint256 amount)
effects: The signature lets the spender (the UniswapX reactor) pull permitted.token from the signer once, up to permitted.amount, until the permit deadline. It uses up the Permit2 nonce.
The signer pays inputToken to the filler. The amount moves from inputStartAmount to inputEndAmount over the decay window, and Permit2 caps it at permitted.amount.

Each output recipient gets outputs[i].token, or native ETH when the token is the zero address. The amount moves down from startAmount to endAmount, so endAmount is the minimum. If a filler other than the exclusive one fills during the exclusivity window, outputs rise by exclusivityOverrideBps.
The order can only be filled before witness.info.deadline and the permit deadline, whichever comes first. The additionalValidationContract can block a fill but moves no assets.
formats.shown: "UniswapX Exclusive Dutch Order", with the spender as raw hex, the permit amount, a 'Spend max' set to inputStartAmount, a minimum amount and raw recipient for each output, and the permit deadline.

findings.title: 'Spend max' shows inputStartAmount, but input can rise to the hidden inputEndAmount.
findings.evidence: descriptor: {"path":"witness.inputStartAmount","label":"Spend max"} while {"path":"witness.inputEndAmount","visible":"never"}. In the UniswapX reactor, the input decays from start to end in either direction. For exact-output orders start < end, so the real maximum is inputEndAmount. Permit2 enforces the bound permitted.amount, which is shown as 'Approve amount', so the true cap is on screen.
findings.fix: Label permitted.amount 'Spend max', or show inputEndAmount next to the start amount (e.g. 'Spend from'/'Spend up to'). Do not call inputStartAmount the max.

findings.title: Intent names the order type, not the swap. No interpolatedIntent says what is sold and bought.
findings.evidence: descriptor: "intent": "UniswapX Exclusive Dutch Order", and there is no interpolatedIntent. A non-expert cannot tell from it that USDC leaves and WETH/ETH comes back (cases 0, 1).
findings.fix: Use intent 'Swap via UniswapX' and an interpolatedIntent such as 'Swap up to {permitted.amount} for at least {witness.outputs.[].endAmount}'.

findings.title: Spender and output recipient are shown as raw hex addresses.
findings.evidence: descriptor: {"path":"spender","label":"Approve to spender","format":"raw"} and {"path":"recipient","label":"On Addresses","format":"raw"}. Cases 0/1 show 0xEf1c6E67... and 0xd8dA6BF2... with no name.
findings.fix: Use format addressName: types ["contract"] for the spender and types ["eoa","wallet"] with sources ["local","ens"] for the recipient.

findings.title: 'Minimum amounts to receive' is applied to every output, including outputs paid to third parties such as fee recipients.
findings.evidence: descriptor: the witness.outputs.[] group labels each endAmount 'Minimum amounts to receive'. UniswapX orders often carry an interface-fee output whose recipient is not the swapper. The recipient is shown, so the outcome is visible.
findings.fix: Relabel to 'Minimum output' and recipient to 'Paid to', so outputs to other parties do not read as received by the signer.

findings.title: Order deadline witness.info.deadline is hidden. Only the permit deadline is shown as 'Approval expire'.
findings.evidence: descriptor: {"path":"witness.info","visible":"never"} and {"path":"deadline","label":"Approval expire"}. In case 0, info.deadline 1777456800 comes before the permit deadline 1777500000, so the order lapses earlier than the time shown.
findings.fix: Add a field for witness.info.deadline, labelled 'Order expires', in date format.

findings.title: Test orders are invalid for the reactor: outputs increase over time and input and outputs both decay.
findings.evidence: cases 0 and 1: outputs startAmount 980000000000000000 < endAmount 1000000000000000000. DutchDecayLib reverts IncorrectAmounts for outputs with start < end. Input 2550→2500 also decays together with the output, which ExclusiveDutchOrderReactor._validateOrder rejects (InputAndOutputDecay). Neither case tests an exact-output order where inputEndAmount > inputStartAmount.
findings.fix: Use realistic orders: an exact-input order (input constant, output start ≥ end) and an exact-output order (output constant, input start < end).
